scope: Page.waitForRequest on native Linux x64, Bun 1.4.2 and stock Chromium headless shell 148.0.7778.96. Focused functionality and packed ESM/CommonJS consumers, not full-core, release or performance admission.

contract.matching: String/glob/RegExp and sync/async Request predicates, with context baseURL for relative strings; URLPattern is not supported.
contract.ownership: Arms the existing native request listener at invocation and returns its original Request before response completion; concurrent matching waits preserve identity.
contract.deadlines: Explicit timeout overrides page then context default; timeout=0 removes the public deadline. Pending callback completion does not extend the deadline or override closure.

candidateChecks: Malformed matchers/deadlines and unknown options reject without listener leaks
Canonical waitForRequest trace call completes independently of trigger

traceVerification.scope: Canonical request-wait API record, original page and successful completion; snapshots/screenshots intentionally disabled.

sourceSnapshot.scope: Original report binds the run snapshot. Later checkpoint, parity and documentation metadata are not part of that snapshot; selected implementation and fixture hashes above remain identical.

attempts.explanation: Initial expectation for a wait started on an already closed page failed against pinned Playwright; retained and classified as the explicit S4.p difference.
Initial 13 shared groups passed; later expanded with repeated URLs, redirect identity, pending callback closure and stronger trace ownership checks.
Expanded 16 shared groups passed on both engines with equal outcomes; trace verification and original watchdog completed successfully.

checks: ESM and CommonJS real request-wait execution
NodeNext MTS and CTS declarations with positive Request inference and negative Response-only member checks
packed.runtimeAcquisition: Explicit existing release-driver override; platform package acquisition was not tested.

cleanup.scope: Disposable install cache and node_modules removed after dependent checks, with archives, locks and evidence retained.

limitations: No speed claim; the native Chromium dependency build ran concurrently.
This new slice has no Node 22/24 or macOS execution evidence.
Existing network delivery scope and bounds apply; this adds no worker or remote-frame coverage.
Crash/browser-teardown and overlapping reentrant predicate races were not separately exercised by this focused fixture.

Trace checks cover one canonical call, its original page, successful completion, independent trigger and absence of duplicate delegated API calls. Snapshots, screenshots and viewer/resource fidelity were not tested here.
